When he felt secure and returned to the road, he stopped at al-Juhfah between Makkah and Madinah, and he recognized the road to Makkah. He longed for it and recalled his birthplace and the birthplaces of his forefathers. Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him and said: "Do you long for your homeland and your birthplace?" He said: "Yes." He said: "God, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, He who ordained for you the Qur'an will surely bring you back to a return,﴾ to Makkah, victorious over it."

Muqatil said: Al-Dahhak said: Ibn Abbas said: It was only revealed at al-Juhfah, neither in Makkah nor in Madinah.

Jabir narrated from Abu Ja'far, who said: My father and I went to Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and he was asked about this verse, ﴿will surely bring you back to a return,﴾ and he said: "To death."

This is also the narration of Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas. Al-Hasan, al-Zuhri and Ikrimah said: "To the Day of Resurrection." Abu Malik and Abu Salih said: "To Paradise."

Ibn Habib informed us, Abd al-Khaliq ibn Ali informed us, he said: Yahya ibn Abi Talib told us, he said: Ammar [in another copy: Hammad ibn Kathir] ibn Kathir informed us, he said: Fudayla [in another copy: from Fadl] informed us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿will surely bring you back to a return﴾: "To Paradise."

﴿Say: My Lord knows best who has brought guidance and who is in clear error.﴾ ﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you, except as a mercy from your Lord.﴾ Some scholars of meanings said: there is inversion and displacement in the sentence; its meaning is: "Indeed He who ordained for you the Qur'an, and you did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you, will surely bring you back to a return." ﴿So never be a supporter of the disbelievers. And let them not turn you away from the signs of God after they have been sent down to you.﴾ This was when they called him to the religion of his forefathers. ﴿And call to your Lord, and never be among the polytheists. And do not invoke with God another deity. There is no deity but Him. Everything will perish except His Face.﴾ That is, except Him, according to Mujahid. Al-Sadiq: His religion. Abu al-'Aliyah: except what is intended by His Face.

Ibn Shadhan [in the Isfahan copy: Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan from Ibn Shadhan] informed us, he said: Ja'iwayh informed us, he said: Salih ibn Muhammad told us, from Jarir, from al-A'mash, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The world will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said: "Separate what was for God from it." So what was for God is separated from it. Then the rest of it is commanded, and it is cast into the Fire.

And from him, from Salih, from Sulayman ibn Amr, from Salim al-Aftas, from al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that a man asked him and he gave him nothing. The man said: "I ask you by the Face of God." Ali said to him: "You have lied. You did not ask me by the Face of God; rather the Face of God is the Truth. Do you not see His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Everything will perish except His Face,﴾ meaning the Truth? But you asked me by your face." [Isfahan copy: "the Creator," al-Dahhak.] "Everything will perish except God, and the Garden, the Fire and the Throne."

Ibn Kaysan: "Except His dominion."

﴿To Him belongs the judgment, and to Him you will be returned.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 28, verses 76–88 (Part 1 of 2)**

Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Musa (Moses). He was his cousin, for Qarun was the son of Yusahir, son of Fahith, son of Lawi, son of Ya'qub (Jacob), while Musa was the son of 'Imran, son of Fahith. This is the view of most exegetes (mufassirun). Ibn Ishaq said: Yusahir son of Fahith married Shamit, daughter of Tabawit, son of Barkiya, son of Yaqshan, son of Ibrahim (Abraham). She bore him 'Imran son of Yusahir and Qarun son of Yusahir. Then [Imran] married Najib, daughter of Samwiya [in the Isfahan manuscript: Shamwil], son of Barkiya, son of Ramnan [in the Isfahan manuscript: Nafshan], son of Barkiya, and she bore him Harun (Aaron) son of 'Imran and Musa son of 'Imran (peace be upon them). So according to Ibn Ishaq's view, Musa was the son of Qarun's brother, and Qarun was his paternal and maternal uncle. Qatadah said: He was called al-Munawwar (the Illuminated) because of his handsome appearance. There was no one among the Children of Israel who recited the Tawrat (Torah) better than him, but the enemy of Allah became a hypocrite, as al-Samiri did.

**"So he oppressed them"**: Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Alawiya related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Isa related to us, from al-Musayyib, regarding "Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Musa, so he oppressed them." He said: He was an agent of Pharaoh over the Children of Israel, and he used to oppress and wrong them. Ibn 'Abbas said: Pharaoh had appointed him over the Children of Israel when he was in Egypt. Sa'id related from Qatadah: "So he oppressed them" through the abundance of his wealth and children. Sufyan [in the Isfahan manuscript: Shaybан] related from him: through arrogance and haughtiness. 'Ata' al-Khurasani and Shahr ibn Hawshab said: He exceeded them in clothing by a span.

**"And We gave him of the treasures such that its keys would be a burden"**: The word *mafatih* is the plural of *miftah*, which is that with which a door is opened.

**"To weigh down a company of strong men"**: That is, it would weigh them down when they carried them because of their heaviness. It is said: *naa yanu'u nawan* when one rises under a heavy load. A poet said:

*Its back-part strains as it rises slowly, and it walks leisurely, then soon pants.* [In the Isfahan manuscript: "then it pants" (fa-nabhara).] [Gharib al-Hadith: 1/321.]

The exegetes differed on the number of the *'usba* (company) in this verse. Mujahid said: between ten and fifteen. Qatadah said: between ten and forty. Abu Salih said: forty men. Ikrimah said: some say forty, and some say seventy. al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: between three and ten. It was also said: sixty.

Jarir related from Mansur, from Khaythama, who said: "I found in the Injil (Gospel) that the keys of Qarun's treasuries were a load for sixty white-faced mules with white markings, and no key exceeded a finger in size, and each key was for one treasure [in the Isfahan manuscript: one treasure-chest]." Mujahid said: The keys were of camel hide. It is said that Qarun, wherever he went, carried the keys to his treasures with him. They were of iron, but when they became heavy on him, they were made of wood, and when these became heavy on him too, he had them made of cowhide, the length of the fingers. They were carried with him when he rode, by forty mules.

Some of them said: By the keys he meant the guards. Abu Salih took this view. Husayn related from Abu Zarin, who said: If one key were for the people of Kufa, it would suffice. He meant only his treasures.

If it is asked: What is the meaning of His saying, "Its keys would be a burden to a company of strong men," when it is the company that bears the keys and not the keys that bear the company? There are two answers. The first is that the keys would incline them and weigh them down with their load. The second is what the people of Basra said: The Arabs do this. They say of a woman, "Her buttocks weigh her down," when in fact it is her buttocks that she bears, as a camel bears its load. A poet said:

*I would ransom him with my own soul and my wealth, and I would not fail you except within my ability.* [Lisan al-'Arab: 5/316.]

The meaning is: I ransom myself and my wealth with him. Another said:

*You ride horses with no leniency between them, and you wear down the spears on the red-skinned fellows.* [Lisan al-'Arab: 4/489.]

It is in fact the red-skinned fellows who are worn down by the spears, and the "horses" here means the men.

**"When his people said to him: Do not exult"**: that is, from among the Children of Israel. "Do not exult" means do not be insolent and do not be boastful. From this is the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: "Indeed, he is exultant and boastful" [Surah Hud: 10]. A poet said:

*I am not one who exults when fortune delights me, nor one who grieves over its changing turns.*  [Zad al-Masir: 6/112.]

He meant: Do not be insolent, for joy is not disliked or blameworthy. **"Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant"**: the insolent, the wanton, the arrogant, those who do not thank Allah, Exalted is He, for what He has given them.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Mansur ibn Ja'far al-Nahawandi related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Nahawandi related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn al-Jarud related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Hayyan related to us, from Nafatih [so in the original], saying: Mubashshir ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: "Do not exult." He said: Do not spread corruption. "Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant": the corrupters. A poet said:

*When you do not cease discharging a trust, and bear another, the deposits have made you exult.* [Kitab al-'Ayn: 3/213.]

He means: have corrupted you.

**"And seek, through what Allah has given you, the Final Abode, and do not forget your share of this world"**: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said: Do not leave off working for your Hereafter in your worldly life until you are saved from the punishment of Allah. This is also the narration of 'Ali ibn Abi Talha from Ibn 'Abbas. 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Do not forget your health, your strength, your youth, your vigor, and your wealth, to seek the Hereafter through them. al-Hasan said: Do not forget to seek, in this world, your sufficiency and wealth from what Allah has made lawful to you.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed me, saying: Hamid ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Harran [in the Isfahan manuscript: al-Khazzaz] related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Salama related to us, saying: Khalaf ibn Khalifa related to us, from Mansur ibn Zadhan, regarding His saying, "and do not forget your share of this world." He said: Your sustenance and the sustenance of your family. It was also said: It is the shroud, for that is his portion of this world when he departs from it.

**"And do good to people as Allah has done good to you, and do not seek corruption in the land. Indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters."** Qarun said: **"I was given this only on account of knowledge that is with me."** That is, on account of a superiority of knowledge that Allah taught me. He saw me as worthy of it, so He preferred me with this wealth over you, because of my superiority over you in knowledge and other things. It was also said: It is the knowledge of alchemy (al-kimya'). Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: Musa (peace be upon him) taught alchemy. He taught a third of that knowledge to Yusha' ibn Nun, a third to Kalib ibn Yufuna [in the Isfahan manuscript: Yufana], and Qarun received a third. Qarun then deceived them until he added their knowledge to his own. In another report: Allah, Exalted is He, taught Musa the knowledge of alchemy, and Musa taught his sister, and his sister taught Qarun, and this was the cause of his words. It was also said: It means knowledge of trading, agriculture, and all kinds of earning and seeking gain, that is with me. It was also said: It concerns the cause of his gathering those riches.

al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Abd Allah informed me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Halwani related to us, saying: Khuzayma ibn Ahmad related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi al-Jawari related to us, saying: I heard Abu Sulayman al-Darani say: Iblis (Satan) appeared to Qarun, and Qarun had remained on a mountain for forty years, worshipping. When he surpassed the Children of Israel in worship, Iblis sent his devils to him, but they could not overcome him. So Iblis himself appeared to him and began to worship as well. Qarun and Iblis competed in worship, and Iblis overpowered him and outdid him, so Qarun submitted to him. Iblis said to him: "O Qarun, we are content with what we are in, but do not witness any gathering of the Children of Israel, do not visit the sick, and do not attend any funeral." Then he brought him down from the mountain to the church, and they were brought food. Iblis said: "O Qarun, we are now content that it should be thus, depending on the Children of Israel." Qarun said to him: "Then what is your opinion?" He said: "Let us earn on Friday and worship for the rest of the Friday." So they earned on Friday and worshipped for the rest of Friday. Then Iblis said to Qarun: "We are content that it should be so." Qarun said to him: "Then what is your opinion?" He said: "Let us earn one day and worship one day, and give in charity and bestow." When they earned one day and worshipped one day, Iblis withdrew and left him, and the world was opened to Qarun, and his wealth grew.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Musa related to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Alawiya related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Musa related to us, from al-Musayyib ibn Shurayk, regarding "whose keys": he said: Their containers. They were four hundred thousand thousand [i.e., four hundred million], in forty sacks.

Allah, Exalted is He, said: **"Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him generations that were more powerful than him and greater in accumulation? And the guilty will not be asked about their sins"** [28:78]. Qatadah said: They will enter the Fire without reckoning. Mujahid said: That is, the angels will not ask about them, because they know them by their marks. al-Hasan said: "The guilty will not be asked about their sins" means that this is known from their predecessors, for if they are questioned, it is a question of rebuke and reproach.

**"So he went out before his people in his adornment"**: Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah [in the Isfahan manuscript: Hammad ibn 'Abd Allah] said: In crimson. al-Nakha'i and al-Hasan said: In red garments. Mujahid said: On white mules with saddles of purple (arjuwan) upon them, and they wore saffron-dyed garments (mu'asfarat). Qatadah said: On four thousand beasts, with them and upon their mounts purple cloth. Ibn Zayd said: With seventy thousand, wearing saffron-dyed garments. He said: That was the first day saffron-dyed garments were seen, as was related to us. Muqatil said: On a grey mule with a golden saddle upon which was purple cloth, and with him four thousand horsemen, and upon their mounts purple cloth, and with him three hundred white slave-girls adorned with jewelry, wearing red garments, on grey mules.

**"Those who desired the life of this world said: Oh, if only we had the like of what Qarun has been given! Indeed, he has a great portion [of wealth]."** **"But those who had been given knowledge said: Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds, and none is granted it except the patient"**, meaning those who are patient in obedience to Allah and in refraining from the adornments of this world.

**"So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home"**. The scholars of ancient reports said: Qarun was the most knowledgeable of the Children of Israel after Musa and Harun, and the most proficient in the Tawrat, and the most handsome and wealthiest of them. But he became a hypocrite like al-Samiri, and so he oppressed his people. The exegetes differed on the meaning of this oppression. Ibn 'Abbas said: Pharaoh had appointed Qarun over the Children of Israel when he was in Egypt. From al-Musayyib ibn Shurayk: he was an agent over the Children of Israel and used to wrong them. It was also said: He exceeded them in clothing by a span. It was said: He oppressed them through arrogance. It was said: Through the abundance of his wealth, for he was the richest and most prosperous of the people of his time. The exegetes differed on the number of the *'usba* in this place. Mujahid said: between ten and fifteen. Qatadah said: between ten and forty. 'Ikrimah said: some say forty and some say seventy. al-Dahhak said: between three and ten. It was said: they were sixty.

It is related from Khuthayma who said: I found in the Injil that the keys of Qarun's treasuries were a load for sixty white-faced mules with white markings, and no key exceeded a finger in size, and each key was for one treasure. It is said: Wherever he went, they were carried with him. They were of iron, but when they became heavy on him, he had them made of wood, and when these became heavy on him, he had them made of cowhide, the length of the fingers. They were carried with him on forty mules. The beginning of his transgression was that he became arrogant and lorded over the people through the abundance of his wealth. He would go out in his finery and strut, as Allah, Exalted is He, said: **"So he went out before his people in his adornment."**

Mujahid said: He went out on white mules with purple saddles, and they wore saffron-dyed garments. 'Abd al-Rahman said: He went out with seventy thousand, wearing saffron-dyed garments. Muqatil said: On a grey mule with a golden saddle upon which was purple cloth, and with him four thousand horsemen, with them and upon their mounts purple cloth, and with him three thousand white slave-girls adorned with jewelry, wearing red garments, on grey mules. So those of ignorance wished for the like of what he had been given, as Allah related. Then the people of knowledge of Allah admonished them: Fear Allah, for the reward of Allah **"is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds."**

He said: Then Allah revealed to His prophet Musa that he should command his people to attach to their cloaks four threads, with a green thread at each end, the color of which is like the color of the sky. Musa summoned the Children of Israel and said to them: Indeed, Allah, Exalted is He, commands you to attach to your cloaks green threads like the color of the sky, so that you may remember your Lord when you see them, and He, Exalted is He, sends down His speech upon you from the sky. Qarun became arrogant and said: These lords only do this to their servants, so that they may be distinguished from others.

When Musa (peace be upon him) brought the Children of Israel across the sea, he appointed al-Hibwara, which is the leadership of the altar and the house of offerings, to Harun. The Children of Israel would bring their gifts and hand them to Harun, who would place them on the altar, and a fire would descend from the sky and consume them. Qarun found this in himself, and he came to Musa and said: "O Musa, to you belongs the messengership, and to Harun the al-Hibwara, and you have nothing of this. I am more learned in the Tawrat than both of you, and I cannot bear this." Musa said: "By Allah, I did not give it to Harun; rather, Allah, Exalted is He, gave it to him." Qarun said: "By Allah, I will not believe you in this until you show me proof of it." So Musa (peace be upon him) gathered the leaders of the Children of Israel and said: "Bring me your staffs." They brought them, and he bound them together and placed them in his tent, where he worshipped Allah, Exalted is He, and they began to guard their staffs until morning. In the morning, Harun's staff had put forth green leaves, and it was from the leaves of an almond tree. Musa said: "O Qarun, do you see this?"

Qarun said: "By Allah, this is no more marvelous than the sorcery you practice."

Qarun left in anger, withdrew from Musa with his followers, and Musa kept dealing gently with him because of the kinship between them, while Qarun harmed him at all times and grew, every day, only in arrogance, defiance, and enmity toward Musa (peace be upon him). He built a house and made its door of gold, and he covered its walls with sheets of gold. The chiefs of the Children of Israel would go to him in the morning and in the evening; he fed them food, they conversed with him, and they laughed with him.

---

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 28, verses 76–88 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Abbas said: Then God, glory be to Him, revealed the zakat (obligatory alms) to Musa (peace be upon him). When God made zakat obligatory for them, Qarun refused. He reached an arrangement with them: for every thousand dinars, one dinar; for every thousand dirhams, one dirham; for every thousand sheep, one sheep; and for every thousand of anything, one of it. Then he returned to his house and calculated his wealth, and found it to be great. His soul would not allow him to give that up. So he gathered the Children of Israel and said to them: "O Children of Israel, Musa has commanded you in everything and you obeyed him, and now he wants to take your wealth." They said to him: "You are our elder and our master, so command us as you wish." He said: "I command you to bring me a certain prostitute, and we will give her a reward on condition that she accuses him of herself. When she does that, the Children of Israel will rise against him and abandon him, and we will be rid of him." So they brought her. Qarun gave her a thousand dirhams. It was also said: a thousand dinars; and it was said: a basin of gold; and it was said: her judgment (or her rule). He said to her: "I will enrich you and mix you with my women, on condition that you accuse Musa of having lain with you tomorrow, when the Children of Israel are present."

When the next day came, Qarun gathered the Children of Israel, then went to Musa and said to him: "The Children of Israel have gathered, waiting for you to come out, so that you may command them and forbid them, and explain to them the signs of their religion and the rulings of their law." Musa went out to them while they were in an open plain. He stood among them and preached, and among what he said in his admonition was: "O Children of Israel, whoever steals, we shall cut off his hand; whoever slanders, we shall flog him eighty lashes; whoever commits fornication while not married, we shall flog him a hundred lashes; and whoever commits fornication while married, we shall stone him until he dies." Qarun said to him: "Even if it is you?" He said: "Even if it is me." Qarun said: "The Children of Israel claim that you committed fornication with such-and-such a woman." He said: "I did?" Qarun said: "Yes." Musa said: "Summon her. If she speaks, then it is as she says." When she came, Musa said to her: "O such-and-such, I did for you what these people say." He was grievous to her, and he adjured her by Him who split the sea for the Children of Israel and sent down the Torah to Musa, to tell the truth. When he adjured her, God came to her aid with success, and she said to herself: "If I repent today, that is better than harming the Messenger of God." So she said: "No, they lie. Rather, Qarun gave me a reward on condition that I accuse you of it myself."

When she spoke these words, Qarun was overcome; he hung his head and the assembly fell silent, and he realized that he had fallen into destruction. Musa fell prostrate, weeping, and said: "O God, if I am Your messenger, then be angry on my behalf." God revealed to him: "Command the earth as you wish, for it is obedient to you." Musa said: "O Children of Israel, God has sent me to Qarun just as He sent me to Pharaoh. Whoever is with him, let him remain in his place; whoever is with me, let him withdraw." So Qarun was left alone, and there remained with him only two men. Then Musa said: "O earth, seize them!" It took them up to their necks. Qarun and his companions, throughout all of this, did not look at him, due to the intensity of his anger against him.

Then he said: "O earth, seize them!" The earth closed over them. God revealed to Musa: "O Musa, how harsh you are! They called on you seventy times and you did not have mercy on them nor relieve them. By My might, if they had called on Me, they would have found Me near and responsive."

Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that he is sinking into the earth each day to the height of a man, and he will keep sinking into it, never reaching its bottom until the Day of Resurrection. They said: The Children of Israel awoke whispering among themselves that Musa had only invoked against Qarun so that he could seize his house, treasures and wealth. So Musa prayed to God that the earth would swallow his house and wealth.

God, glory be to Him, revealed to Musa: "I will never again make the earth obedient to anyone after you." This is His saying, exalted be He: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his house. He had no party to help him against God, nor was he among those who could defend themselves.﴾ ﴿And those who had desired his position the day before began to say, "Woe! It is indeed God who extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it. Had God not been gracious to us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us. Woe! Indeed, the disbelievers never prosper."﴾

The Arabs use ﴿aṣbaḥa﴾, ﴿amsā﴾ and ﴿aḍḥā﴾ (to become in the morning, evening and forenoon) to express a change of state and action; so they say: "So-and-so became a worker (aṣbaḥa ʿāmilan), became sad in the evening (amsā ḥazīnan), became destitute at midday (aḍḥā muʿdaman)," when they have come to these conditions, and there is no morning, evening or forenoon in the matter at all.

﴿Wayka-anna Allāh﴾ (Woe! It is indeed God): The scholars differed over this expression. Mujahid said: its meaning is, "Do you not know?" Qatada said: "Do you not see?" Al-Farra' said: it is a word of confirmation, like a man saying: "Do you not see the making and kindness of God?" It was mentioned that someone told him that he heard a Bedouin woman say to her husband: "Where is your son?" He said: "Wayka-annahu wara'a al-bayt," meaning: "Do you not see him behind the house?" Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan said: it is a word of beginning and affirmation, its meaning being: "Indeed God extends provision." Al-Mubarrad said: it expresses wonder. Qutrub said: it is only "waylaka" (woe to you), with the lam dropped. Antarah said:

"The words of the horsemen, 'Woe to you, Antarah, advance!' have healed my soul and cured its sickness."

It was also said: it is an exclamation of alertness, like "alā" and "amā." One of the poets said:

"Wayka-anna he who has wealth is loved, while he who is poor lives a life of hardship."

Al-Qutaybi said: its meaning is "mercy" in the language of Himyar. Sibawayh said: I asked al-Khalil about it, and he said: "Way" is an exclamation of alertness, separated from ﴿kaʾanna﴾, and ﴿kaʾanna﴾ carries the meaning of "it seems" and "knowledge."

﴿He extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it (yaqdiru, meaning: constricts).﴾ ﴿Had God not been gracious to us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us.﴾ Yaʿqūb, some of the people of Syria and the people of Kufa read ﴿lakhasafa﴾ with a fatḥa on the kh and s; the common reading is with a ḍamma on the kh and a kasra on the s. ﴿Wayka-annahu lā yufliḥu al-kāfirūn (woe, indeed the disbelievers never prosper).﴾ ﴿That is the abode of the Hereafter. We assign it to those who do not desire haughtiness in the earth﴾, meaning arrogance and tyranny in it, ﴿nor corruption﴾, meaning working in acts of disobedience. This is from Ibn Jurayj, Muqatil, Ikrimah and Muslim al-Batin. [Note: as in the original.] Corruption: taking wealth unjustly. Al-Kalbi said: it means calling people to other than the worship of God.

﴿And the good end is for the God-conscious.﴾ Qatada said: it is Paradise. ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it, and whoever brings an evil deed, those who committed evil deeds will not be recompensed except for what they used to do.﴾ ﴿Indeed, He who ordained for you the Qur'an will surely bring you back to a return (maʿād).﴾ According to most exegetes (tafsir), this means: He who revealed it. Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: it means He made it obligatory for you to act upon the Qur'an. ﴿Surely He will bring you back to a place of return.﴾ Al-Dahhak and Mujahid said: to Makkah. This is also the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Qutaybah [in the manuscript a word resembling "al-Qutaybi" appears; what is written here is from Zad al-Masir, 6/120] said: the maʿād of a man is his homeland, because he departs and then returns to his homeland.

Muqatil said: The Prophet (peace be upon him) left the cave by night, then emigrated directly toward Madinah. He traveled off the main road for fear of pursuit. When he felt secure and returned to the road, he stopped at al-Juhfah between Makkah and Madinah, and he recognized the road to Makkah. He longed for it and recalled his birthplace and the birthplaces of his forefathers. Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him and said: "Do you long for your homeland and your birthplace?" He said: "Yes." He said: "God, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, He who ordained for you the Qur'an will surely bring you back to a return,﴾ to Makkah, victorious over it."

Muqatil said: Al-Dahhak said: Ibn Abbas said: It was only revealed at al-Juhfah, neither in Makkah nor in Madinah.

Jabir narrated from Abu Ja'far, who said: My father and I went to Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and he was asked about this verse, ﴿will surely bring you back to a return,﴾ and he said: "To death."

This is also the narration of Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas. Al-Hasan, al-Zuhri and Ikrimah said: "To the Day of Resurrection." Abu Malik and Abu Salih said: "To Paradise."

Ibn Habib informed us, Abd al-Khaliq ibn Ali informed us, he said: Yahya ibn Abi Talib told us, he said: Ammar [in another copy: Hammad ibn Kathir] ibn Kathir informed us, he said: Fudayla [in another copy: from Fadl] informed us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿will surely bring you back to a return﴾: "To Paradise."

﴿Say: My Lord knows best who has brought guidance and who is in clear error.﴾ ﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you, except as a mercy from your Lord.﴾ Some scholars of meanings said: there is inversion and displacement in the sentence; its meaning is: "Indeed He who ordained for you the Qur'an, and you did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you, will surely bring you back to a return." ﴿So never be a supporter of the disbelievers. And let them not turn you away from the signs of God after they have been sent down to you.﴾ This was when they called him to the religion of his forefathers. ﴿And call to your Lord, and never be among the polytheists. And do not invoke with God another deity. There is no deity but Him. Everything will perish except His Face.﴾ That is, except Him, according to Mujahid. Al-Sadiq: His religion. Abu al-'Aliyah: except what is intended by His Face.

Ibn Shadhan [in the Isfahan copy: Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan from Ibn Shadhan] informed us, he said: Ja'iwayh informed us, he said: Salih ibn Muhammad told us, from Jarir, from al-A'mash, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The world will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said: "Separate what was for God from it." So what was for God is separated from it. Then the rest of it is commanded, and it is cast into the Fire.

And from him, from Salih, from Sulayman ibn Amr, from Salim al-Aftas, from al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that a man asked him and he gave him nothing. The man said: "I ask you by the Face of God." Ali said to him: "You have lied. You did not ask me by the Face of God; rather the Face of God is the Truth. Do you not see His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Everything will perish except His Face,﴾ meaning the Truth? But you asked me by your face." [Isfahan copy: "the Creator," al-Dahhak.] "Everything will perish except God, and the Garden, the Fire and the Throne."

Ibn Kaysan: "Except His dominion."

﴿To Him belongs the judgment, and to Him you will be returned.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 28, verses 76–88 (Part 1 of 2)**

Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Musa (Moses). He was his cousin, for Qarun was the son of Yusahir, son of Fahith, son of Lawi, son of Ya'qub (Jacob), while Musa was the son of 'Imran, son of Fahith. This is the view of most exegetes (mufassirun). Ibn Ishaq said: Yusahir son of Fahith married Shamit, daughter of Tabawit, son of Barkiya, son of Yaqshan, son of Ibrahim (Abraham). She bore him 'Imran son of Yusahir and Qarun son of Yusahir. Then [Imran] married Najib, daughter of Samwiya [in the Isfahan manuscript: Shamwil], son of Barkiya, son of Ramnan [in the Isfahan manuscript: Nafshan], son of Barkiya, and she bore him Harun (Aaron) son of 'Imran and Musa son of 'Imran (peace be upon them). So according to Ibn Ishaq's view, Musa was the son of Qarun's brother, and Qarun was his paternal and maternal uncle. Qatadah said: He was called al-Munawwar (the Illuminated) because of his handsome appearance. There was no one among the Children of Israel who recited the Tawrat (Torah) better than him, but the enemy of Allah became a hypocrite, as al-Samiri did.

**"So he oppressed them"**: Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Alawiya related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Isa related to us, from al-Musayyib, regarding "Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Musa, so he oppressed them." He said: He was an agent of Pharaoh over the Children of Israel, and he used to oppress and wrong them. Ibn 'Abbas said: Pharaoh had appointed him over the Children of Israel when he was in Egypt. Sa'id related from Qatadah: "So he oppressed them" through the abundance of his wealth and children. Sufyan [in the Isfahan manuscript: Shaybан] related from him: through arrogance and haughtiness. 'Ata' al-Khurasani and Shahr ibn Hawshab said: He exceeded them in clothing by a span.

**"And We gave him of the treasures such that its keys would be a burden"**: The word *mafatih* is the plural of *miftah*, which is that with which a door is opened.

**"To weigh down a company of strong men"**: That is, it would weigh them down when they carried them because of their heaviness. It is said: *naa yanu'u nawan* when one rises under a heavy load. A poet said:

*Its back-part strains as it rises slowly, and it walks leisurely, then soon pants.* [In the Isfahan manuscript: "then it pants" (fa-nabhara).] [Gharib al-Hadith: 1/321.]

The exegetes differed on the number of the *'usba* (company) in this verse. Mujahid said: between ten and fifteen. Qatadah said: between ten and forty. Abu Salih said: forty men. Ikrimah said: some say forty, and some say seventy. al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: between three and ten. It was also said: sixty.

Jarir related from Mansur, from Khaythama, who said: "I found in the Injil (Gospel) that the keys of Qarun's treasuries were a load for sixty white-faced mules with white markings, and no key exceeded a finger in size, and each key was for one treasure [in the Isfahan manuscript: one treasure-chest]." Mujahid said: The keys were of camel hide. It is said that Qarun, wherever he went, carried the keys to his treasures with him. They were of iron, but when they became heavy on him, they were made of wood, and when these became heavy on him too, he had them made of cowhide, the length of the fingers. They were carried with him when he rode, by forty mules.

Some of them said: By the keys he meant the guards. Abu Salih took this view. Husayn related from Abu Zarin, who said: If one key were for the people of Kufa, it would suffice. He meant only his treasures.

If it is asked: What is the meaning of His saying, "Its keys would be a burden to a company of strong men," when it is the company that bears the keys and not the keys that bear the company? There are two answers. The first is that the keys would incline them and weigh them down with their load. The second is what the people of Basra said: The Arabs do this. They say of a woman, "Her buttocks weigh her down," when in fact it is her buttocks that she bears, as a camel bears its load. A poet said:

*I would ransom him with my own soul and my wealth, and I would not fail you except within my ability.* [Lisan al-'Arab: 5/316.]

The meaning is: I ransom myself and my wealth with him. Another said:

*You ride horses with no leniency between them, and you wear down the spears on the red-skinned fellows.* [Lisan al-'Arab: 4/489.]

It is in fact the red-skinned fellows who are worn down by the spears, and the "horses" here means the men.

**"When his people said to him: Do not exult"**: that is, from among the Children of Israel. "Do not exult" means do not be insolent and do not be boastful. From this is the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: "Indeed, he is exultant and boastful" [Surah Hud: 10]. A poet said:

*I am not one who exults when fortune delights me, nor one who grieves over its changing turns.*  [Zad al-Masir: 6/112.]

He meant: Do not be insolent, for joy is not disliked or blameworthy. **"Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant"**: the insolent, the wanton, the arrogant, those who do not thank Allah, Exalted is He, for what He has given them.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Mansur ibn Ja'far al-Nahawandi related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Nahawandi related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn al-Jarud related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Hayyan related to us, from Nafatih [so in the original], saying: Mubashshir ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: "Do not exult." He said: Do not spread corruption. "Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant": the corrupters. A poet said:

*When you do not cease discharging a trust, and bear another, the deposits have made you exult.* [Kitab al-'Ayn: 3/213.]

He means: have corrupted you.

**"And seek, through what Allah has given you, the Final Abode, and do not forget your share of this world"**: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said: Do not leave off working for your Hereafter in your worldly life until you are saved from the punishment of Allah. This is also the narration of 'Ali ibn Abi Talha from Ibn 'Abbas. 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Do not forget your health, your strength, your youth, your vigor, and your wealth, to seek the Hereafter through them. al-Hasan said: Do not forget to seek, in this world, your sufficiency and wealth from what Allah has made lawful to you.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed me, saying: Hamid ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Harran [in the Isfahan manuscript: al-Khazzaz] related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Salama related to us, saying: Khalaf ibn Khalifa related to us, from Mansur ibn Zadhan, regarding His saying, "and do not forget your share of this world." He said: Your sustenance and the sustenance of your family. It was also said: It is the shroud, for that is his portion of this world when he departs from it.

**"And do good to people as Allah has done good to you, and do not seek corruption in the land. Indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters."** Qarun said: **"I was given this only on account of knowledge that is with me."** That is, on account of a superiority of knowledge that Allah taught me. He saw me as worthy of it, so He preferred me with this wealth over you, because of my superiority over you in knowledge and other things. It was also said: It is the knowledge of alchemy (al-kimya'). Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: Musa (peace be upon him) taught alchemy. He taught a third of that knowledge to Yusha' ibn Nun, a third to Kalib ibn Yufuna [in the Isfahan manuscript: Yufana], and Qarun received a third. Qarun then deceived them until he added their knowledge to his own. In another report: Allah, Exalted is He, taught Musa the knowledge of alchemy, and Musa taught his sister, and his sister taught Qarun, and this was the cause of his words. It was also said: It means knowledge of trading, agriculture, and all kinds of earning and seeking gain, that is with me. It was also said: It concerns the cause of his gathering those riches.

al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Abd Allah informed me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Halwani related to us, saying: Khuzayma ibn Ahmad related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi al-Jawari related to us, saying: I heard Abu Sulayman al-Darani say: Iblis (Satan) appeared to Qarun, and Qarun had remained on a mountain for forty years, worshipping. When he surpassed the Children of Israel in worship, Iblis sent his devils to him, but they could not overcome him. So Iblis himself appeared to him and began to worship as well. Qarun and Iblis competed in worship, and Iblis overpowered him and outdid him, so Qarun submitted to him. Iblis said to him: "O Qarun, we are content with what we are in, but do not witness any gathering of the Children of Israel, do not visit the sick, and do not attend any funeral." Then he brought him down from the mountain to the church, and they were brought food. Iblis said: "O Qarun, we are now content that it should be thus, depending on the Children of Israel." Qarun said to him: "Then what is your opinion?" He said: "Let us earn on Friday and worship for the rest of the Friday." So they earned on Friday and worshipped for the rest of Friday. Then Iblis said to Qarun: "We are content that it should be so." Qarun said to him: "Then what is your opinion?" He said: "Let us earn one day and worship one day, and give in charity and bestow." When they earned one day and worshipped one day, Iblis withdrew and left him, and the world was opened to Qarun, and his wealth grew.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Musa related to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Alawiya related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Musa related to us, from al-Musayyib ibn Shurayk, regarding "whose keys": he said: Their containers. They were four hundred thousand thousand [i.e., four hundred million], in forty sacks.

Allah, Exalted is He, said: **"Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him generations that were more powerful than him and greater in accumulation? And the guilty will not be asked about their sins"** [28:78]. Qatadah said: They will enter the Fire without reckoning. Mujahid said: That is, the angels will not ask about them, because they know them by their marks. al-Hasan said: "The guilty will not be asked about their sins" means that this is known from their predecessors, for if they are questioned, it is a question of rebuke and reproach.

**"So he went out before his people in his adornment"**: Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah [in the Isfahan manuscript: Hammad ibn 'Abd Allah] said: In crimson. al-Nakha'i and al-Hasan said: In red garments. Mujahid said: On white mules with saddles of purple (arjuwan) upon them, and they wore saffron-dyed garments (mu'asfarat). Qatadah said: On four thousand beasts, with them and upon their mounts purple cloth. Ibn Zayd said: With seventy thousand, wearing saffron-dyed garments. He said: That was the first day saffron-dyed garments were seen, as was related to us. Muqatil said: On a grey mule with a golden saddle upon which was purple cloth, and with him four thousand horsemen, and upon their mounts purple cloth, and with him three hundred white slave-girls adorned with jewelry, wearing red garments, on grey mules.

**"Those who desired the life of this world said: Oh, if only we had the like of what Qarun has been given! Indeed, he has a great portion [of wealth]."** **"But those who had been given knowledge said: Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds, and none is granted it except the patient"**, meaning those who are patient in obedience to Allah and in refraining from the adornments of this world.

**"So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home"**. The scholars of ancient reports said: Qarun was the most knowledgeable of the Children of Israel after Musa and Harun, and the most proficient in the Tawrat, and the most handsome and wealthiest of them. But he became a hypocrite like al-Samiri, and so he oppressed his people. The exegetes differed on the meaning of this oppression. Ibn 'Abbas said: Pharaoh had appointed Qarun over the Children of Israel when he was in Egypt. From al-Musayyib ibn Shurayk: he was an agent over the Children of Israel and used to wrong them. It was also said: He exceeded them in clothing by a span. It was said: He oppressed them through arrogance. It was said: Through the abundance of his wealth, for he was the richest and most prosperous of the people of his time. The exegetes differed on the number of the *'usba* in this place. Mujahid said: between ten and fifteen. Qatadah said: between ten and forty. 'Ikrimah said: some say forty and some say seventy. al-Dahhak said: between three and ten. It was said: they were sixty.

It is related from Khuthayma who said: I found in the Injil that the keys of Qarun's treasuries were a load for sixty white-faced mules with white markings, and no key exceeded a finger in size, and each key was for one treasure. It is said: Wherever he went, they were carried with him. They were of iron, but when they became heavy on him, he had them made of wood, and when these became heavy on him, he had them made of cowhide, the length of the fingers. They were carried with him on forty mules. The beginning of his transgression was that he became arrogant and lorded over the people through the abundance of his wealth. He would go out in his finery and strut, as Allah, Exalted is He, said: **"So he went out before his people in his adornment."**

Mujahid said: He went out on white mules with purple saddles, and they wore saffron-dyed garments. 'Abd al-Rahman said: He went out with seventy thousand, wearing saffron-dyed garments. Muqatil said: On a grey mule with a golden saddle upon which was purple cloth, and with him four thousand horsemen, with them and upon their mounts purple cloth, and with him three thousand white slave-girls adorned with jewelry, wearing red garments, on grey mules. So those of ignorance wished for the like of what he had been given, as Allah related. Then the people of knowledge of Allah admonished them: Fear Allah, for the reward of Allah **"is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds."**

He said: Then Allah revealed to His prophet Musa that he should command his people to attach to their cloaks four threads, with a green thread at each end, the color of which is like the color of the sky. Musa summoned the Children of Israel and said to them: Indeed, Allah, Exalted is He, commands you to attach to your cloaks green threads like the color of the sky, so that you may remember your Lord when you see them, and He, Exalted is He, sends down His speech upon you from the sky. Qarun became arrogant and said: These lords only do this to their servants, so that they may be distinguished from others.

When Musa (peace be upon him) brought the Children of Israel across the sea, he appointed al-Hibwara, which is the leadership of the altar and the house of offerings, to Harun. The Children of Israel would bring their gifts and hand them to Harun, who would place them on the altar, and a fire would descend from the sky and consume them. Qarun found this in himself, and he came to Musa and said: "O Musa, to you belongs the messengership, and to Harun the al-Hibwara, and you have nothing of this. I am more learned in the Tawrat than both of you, and I cannot bear this." Musa said: "By Allah, I did not give it to Harun; rather, Allah, Exalted is He, gave it to him." Qarun said: "By Allah, I will not believe you in this until you show me proof of it." So Musa (peace be upon him) gathered the leaders of the Children of Israel and said: "Bring me your staffs." They brought them, and he bound them together and placed them in his tent, where he worshipped Allah, Exalted is He, and they began to guard their staffs until morning. In the morning, Harun's staff had put forth green leaves, and it was from the leaves of an almond tree. Musa said: "O Qarun, do you see this?"

Qarun said: "By Allah, this is no more marvelous than the sorcery you practice."

Qarun left in anger, withdrew from Musa with his followers, and Musa kept dealing gently with him because of the kinship between them, while Qarun harmed him at all times and grew, every day, only in arrogance, defiance, and enmity toward Musa (peace be upon him). He built a house and made its door of gold, and he covered its walls with sheets of gold. The chiefs of the Children of Israel would go to him in the morning and in the evening; he fed them food, they conversed with him, and they laughed with him.

---

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 28, verses 76–88 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Abbas said: Then God, glory be to Him, revealed the zakat (obligatory alms) to Musa (peace be upon him). When God made zakat obligatory for them, Qarun refused. He reached an arrangement with them: for every thousand dinars, one dinar; for every thousand dirhams, one dirham; for every thousand sheep, one sheep; and for every thousand of anything, one of it. Then he returned to his house and calculated his wealth, and found it to be great. His soul would not allow him to give that up. So he gathered the Children of Israel and said to them: "O Children of Israel, Musa has commanded you in everything and you obeyed him, and now he wants to take your wealth." They said to him: "You are our elder and our master, so command us as you wish." He said: "I command you to bring me a certain prostitute, and we will give her a reward on condition that she accuses him of herself. When she does that, the Children of Israel will rise against him and abandon him, and we will be rid of him." So they brought her. Qarun gave her a thousand dirhams. It was also said: a thousand dinars; and it was said: a basin of gold; and it was said: her judgment (or her rule). He said to her: "I will enrich you and mix you with my women, on condition that you accuse Musa of having lain with you tomorrow, when the Children of Israel are present."

When the next day came, Qarun gathered the Children of Israel, then went to Musa and said to him: "The Children of Israel have gathered, waiting for you to come out, so that you may command them and forbid them, and explain to them the signs of their religion and the rulings of their law." Musa went out to them while they were in an open plain. He stood among them and preached, and among what he said in his admonition was: "O Children of Israel, whoever steals, we shall cut off his hand; whoever slanders, we shall flog him eighty lashes; whoever commits fornication while not married, we shall flog him a hundred lashes; and whoever commits fornication while married, we shall stone him until he dies." Qarun said to him: "Even if it is you?" He said: "Even if it is me." Qarun said: "The Children of Israel claim that you committed fornication with such-and-such a woman." He said: "I did?" Qarun said: "Yes." Musa said: "Summon her. If she speaks, then it is as she says." When she came, Musa said to her: "O such-and-such, I did for you what these people say." He was grievous to her, and he adjured her by Him who split the sea for the Children of Israel and sent down the Torah to Musa, to tell the truth. When he adjured her, God came to her aid with success, and she said to herself: "If I repent today, that is better than harming the Messenger of God." So she said: "No, they lie. Rather, Qarun gave me a reward on condition that I accuse you of it myself."

When she spoke these words, Qarun was overcome; he hung his head and the assembly fell silent, and he realized that he had fallen into destruction. Musa fell prostrate, weeping, and said: "O God, if I am Your messenger, then be angry on my behalf." God revealed to him: "Command the earth as you wish, for it is obedient to you." Musa said: "O Children of Israel, God has sent me to Qarun just as He sent me to Pharaoh. Whoever is with him, let him remain in his place; whoever is with me, let him withdraw." So Qarun was left alone, and there remained with him only two men. Then Musa said: "O earth, seize them!" It took them up to their necks. Qarun and his companions, throughout all of this, did not look at him, due to the intensity of his anger against him.

Then he said: "O earth, seize them!" The earth closed over them. God revealed to Musa: "O Musa, how harsh you are! They called on you seventy times and you did not have mercy on them nor relieve them. By My might, if they had called on Me, they would have found Me near and responsive."

Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that he is sinking into the earth each day to the height of a man, and he will keep sinking into it, never reaching its bottom until the Day of Resurrection. They said: The Children of Israel awoke whispering among themselves that Musa had only invoked against Qarun so that he could seize his house, treasures and wealth. So Musa prayed to God that the earth would swallow his house and wealth.

God, glory be to Him, revealed to Musa: "I will never again make the earth obedient to anyone after you." This is His saying, exalted be He: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his house. He had no party to help him against God, nor was he among those who could defend themselves.﴾ ﴿And those who had desired his position the day before began to say, "Woe! It is indeed God who extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it. Had God not been gracious to us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us. Woe! Indeed, the disbelievers never prosper."﴾

The Arabs use ﴿aṣbaḥa﴾, ﴿amsā﴾ and ﴿aḍḥā﴾ (to become in the morning, evening and forenoon) to express a change of state and action; so they say: "So-and-so became a worker (aṣbaḥa ʿāmilan), became sad in the evening (amsā ḥazīnan), became destitute at midday (aḍḥā muʿdaman)," when they have come to these conditions, and there is no morning, evening or forenoon in the matter at all.

﴿Wayka-anna Allāh﴾ (Woe! It is indeed God): The scholars differed over this expression. Mujahid said: its meaning is, "Do you not know?" Qatada said: "Do you not see?" Al-Farra' said: it is a word of confirmation, like a man saying: "Do you not see the making and kindness of God?" It was mentioned that someone told him that he heard a Bedouin woman say to her husband: "Where is your son?" He said: "Wayka-annahu wara'a al-bayt," meaning: "Do you not see him behind the house?" Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan said: it is a word of beginning and affirmation, its meaning being: "Indeed God extends provision." Al-Mubarrad said: it expresses wonder. Qutrub said: it is only "waylaka" (woe to you), with the lam dropped. Antarah said:

"The words of the horsemen, 'Woe to you, Antarah, advance!' have healed my soul and cured its sickness."

It was also said: it is an exclamation of alertness, like "alā" and "amā." One of the poets said:

"Wayka-anna he who has wealth is loved, while he who is poor lives a life of hardship."

Al-Qutaybi said: its meaning is "mercy" in the language of Himyar. Sibawayh said: I asked al-Khalil about it, and he said: "Way" is an exclamation of alertness, separated from ﴿kaʾanna﴾, and ﴿kaʾanna﴾ carries the meaning of "it seems" and "knowledge."

﴿He extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it (yaqdiru, meaning: constricts).﴾ ﴿Had God not been gracious to us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us.﴾ Yaʿqūb, some of the people of Syria and the people of Kufa read ﴿lakhasafa﴾ with a fatḥa on the kh and s; the common reading is with a ḍamma on the kh and a kasra on the s. ﴿Wayka-annahu lā yufliḥu al-kāfirūn (woe, indeed the disbelievers never prosper).﴾ ﴿That is the abode of the Hereafter. We assign it to those who do not desire haughtiness in the earth﴾, meaning arrogance and tyranny in it, ﴿nor corruption﴾, meaning working in acts of disobedience. This is from Ibn Jurayj, Muqatil, Ikrimah and Muslim al-Batin. [Note: as in the original.] Corruption: taking wealth unjustly. Al-Kalbi said: it means calling people to other than the worship of God.

﴿And the good end is for the God-conscious.﴾ Qatada said: it is Paradise. ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it, and whoever brings an evil deed, those who committed evil deeds will not be recompensed except for what they used to do.﴾ ﴿Indeed, He who ordained for you the Qur'an will surely bring you back to a return (maʿād).﴾ According to most exegetes (tafsir), this means: He who revealed it. Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: it means He made it obligatory for you to act upon the Qur'an. ﴿Surely He will bring you back to a place of return.﴾ Al-Dahhak and Mujahid said: to Makkah. This is also the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Qutaybah [in the manuscript a word resembling "al-Qutaybi" appears; what is written here is from Zad al-Masir, 6/120] said: the maʿād of a man is his homeland, because he departs and then returns to his homeland.

Muqatil said: The Prophet (peace be upon him) left the cave by night, then emigrated directly toward Madinah. He traveled off the main road for fear of pursuit. When he felt secure and returned to the road, he stopped at al-Juhfah between Makkah and Madinah, and he recognized the road to Makkah. He longed for it and recalled his birthplace and the birthplaces of his forefathers. Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him and said: "Do you long for your homeland and your birthplace?" He said: "Yes." He said: "God, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, He who ordained for you the Qur'an will surely bring you back to a return,﴾ to Makkah, victorious over it."

Muqatil said: Al-Dahhak said: Ibn Abbas said: It was only revealed at al-Juhfah, neither in Makkah nor in Madinah.

Jabir narrated from Abu Ja'far, who said: My father and I went to Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and he was asked about this verse, ﴿will surely bring you back to a return,﴾ and he said: "To death."

This is also the narration of Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas. Al-Hasan, al-Zuhri and Ikrimah said: "To the Day of Resurrection." Abu Malik and Abu Salih said: "To Paradise."

Ibn Habib informed us, Abd al-Khaliq ibn Ali informed us, he said: Yahya ibn Abi Talib told us, he said: Ammar [in another copy: Hammad ibn Kathir] ibn Kathir informed us, he said: Fudayla [in another copy: from Fadl] informed us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿will surely bring you back to a return﴾: "To Paradise."

﴿Say: My Lord knows best who has brought guidance and who is in clear error.﴾ ﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you, except as a mercy from your Lord.﴾ Some scholars of meanings said: there is inversion and displacement in the sentence; its meaning is: "Indeed He who ordained for you the Qur'an, and you did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you, will surely bring you back to a return." ﴿So never be a supporter of the disbelievers. And let them not turn you away from the signs of God after they have been sent down to you.﴾ This was when they called him to the religion of his forefathers. ﴿And call to your Lord, and never be among the polytheists. And do not invoke with God another deity. There is no deity but Him. Everything will perish except His Face.﴾ That is, except Him, according to Mujahid. Al-Sadiq: His religion. Abu al-'Aliyah: except what is intended by His Face.

Ibn Shadhan [in the Isfahan copy: Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan from Ibn Shadhan] informed us, he said: Ja'iwayh informed us, he said: Salih ibn Muhammad told us, from Jarir, from al-A'mash, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The world will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said: "Separate what was for God from it." So what was for God is separated from it. Then the rest of it is commanded, and it is cast into the Fire.

And from him, from Salih, from Sulayman ibn Amr, from Salim al-Aftas, from al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that a man asked him and he gave him nothing. The man said: "I ask you by the Face of God." Ali said to him: "You have lied. You did not ask me by the Face of God; rather the Face of God is the Truth. Do you not see His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Everything will perish except His Face,﴾ meaning the Truth? But you asked me by your face." [Isfahan copy: "the Creator," al-Dahhak.] "Everything will perish except God, and the Garden, the Fire and the Throne."

Ibn Kaysan: "Except His dominion."

﴿To Him belongs the judgment, and to Him you will be returned.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 28, verses 76–88 (Part 1 of 2)**

Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Musa (Moses). He was his cousin, for Qarun was the son of Yusahir, son of Fahith, son of Lawi, son of Ya'qub (Jacob), while Musa was the son of 'Imran, son of Fahith. This is the view of most exegetes (mufassirun). Ibn Ishaq said: Yusahir son of Fahith married Shamit, daughter of Tabawit, son of Barkiya, son of Yaqshan, son of Ibrahim (Abraham). She bore him 'Imran son of Yusahir and Qarun son of Yusahir. Then [Imran] married Najib, daughter of Samwiya [in the Isfahan manuscript: Shamwil], son of Barkiya, son of Ramnan [in the Isfahan manuscript: Nafshan], son of Barkiya, and she bore him Harun (Aaron) son of 'Imran and Musa son of 'Imran (peace be upon them). So according to Ibn Ishaq's view, Musa was the son of Qarun's brother, and Qarun was his paternal and maternal uncle. Qatadah said: He was called al-Munawwar (the Illuminated) because of his handsome appearance. There was no one among the Children of Israel who recited the Tawrat (Torah) better than him, but the enemy of Allah became a hypocrite, as al-Samiri did.

**"So he oppressed them"**: Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Alawiya related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Isa related to us, from al-Musayyib, regarding "Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Musa, so he oppressed them." He said: He was an agent of Pharaoh over the Children of Israel, and he used to oppress and wrong them. Ibn 'Abbas said: Pharaoh had appointed him over the Children of Israel when he was in Egypt. Sa'id related from Qatadah: "So he oppressed them" through the abundance of his wealth and children. Sufyan [in the Isfahan manuscript: Shaybан] related from him: through arrogance and haughtiness. 'Ata' al-Khurasani and Shahr ibn Hawshab said: He exceeded them in clothing by a span.

**"And We gave him of the treasures such that its keys would be a burden"**: The word *mafatih* is the plural of *miftah*, which is that with which a door is opened.

**"To weigh down a company of strong men"**: That is, it would weigh them down when they carried them because of their heaviness. It is said: *naa yanu'u nawan* when one rises under a heavy load. A poet said:

*Its back-part strains as it rises slowly, and it walks leisurely, then soon pants.* [In the Isfahan manuscript: "then it pants" (fa-nabhara).] [Gharib al-Hadith: 1/321.]

The exegetes differed on the number of the *'usba* (company) in this verse. Mujahid said: between ten and fifteen. Qatadah said: between ten and forty. Abu Salih said: forty men. Ikrimah said: some say forty, and some say seventy. al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: between three and ten. It was also said: sixty.

Jarir related from Mansur, from Khaythama, who said: "I found in the Injil (Gospel) that the keys of Qarun's treasuries were a load for sixty white-faced mules with white markings, and no key exceeded a finger in size, and each key was for one treasure [in the Isfahan manuscript: one treasure-chest]." Mujahid said: The keys were of camel hide. It is said that Qarun, wherever he went, carried the keys to his treasures with him. They were of iron, but when they became heavy on him, they were made of wood, and when these became heavy on him too, he had them made of cowhide, the length of the fingers. They were carried with him when he rode, by forty mules.

Some of them said: By the keys he meant the guards. Abu Salih took this view. Husayn related from Abu Zarin, who said: If one key were for the people of Kufa, it would suffice. He meant only his treasures.

If it is asked: What is the meaning of His saying, "Its keys would be a burden to a company of strong men," when it is the company that bears the keys and not the keys that bear the company? There are two answers. The first is that the keys would incline them and weigh them down with their load. The second is what the people of Basra said: The Arabs do this. They say of a woman, "Her buttocks weigh her down," when in fact it is her buttocks that she bears, as a camel bears its load. A poet said:

*I would ransom him with my own soul and my wealth, and I would not fail you except within my ability.* [Lisan al-'Arab: 5/316.]

The meaning is: I ransom myself and my wealth with him. Another said:

*You ride horses with no leniency between them, and you wear down the spears on the red-skinned fellows.* [Lisan al-'Arab: 4/489.]

It is in fact the red-skinned fellows who are worn down by the spears, and the "horses" here means the men.

**"When his people said to him: Do not exult"**: that is, from among the Children of Israel. "Do not exult" means do not be insolent and do not be boastful. From this is the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: "Indeed, he is exultant and boastful" [Surah Hud: 10]. A poet said:

*I am not one who exults when fortune delights me, nor one who grieves over its changing turns.*  [Zad al-Masir: 6/112.]

He meant: Do not be insolent, for joy is not disliked or blameworthy. **"Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant"**: the insolent, the wanton, the arrogant, those who do not thank Allah, Exalted is He, for what He has given them.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Mansur ibn Ja'far al-Nahawandi related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Nahawandi related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn al-Jarud related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Hayyan related to us, from Nafatih [so in the original], saying: Mubashshir ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: "Do not exult." He said: Do not spread corruption. "Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant": the corrupters. A poet said:

*When you do not cease discharging a trust, and bear another, the deposits have made you exult.* [Kitab al-'Ayn: 3/213.]

He means: have corrupted you.

**"And seek, through what Allah has given you, the Final Abode, and do not forget your share of this world"**: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said: Do not leave off working for your Hereafter in your worldly life until you are saved from the punishment of Allah. This is also the narration of 'Ali ibn Abi Talha from Ibn 'Abbas. 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Do not forget your health, your strength, your youth, your vigor, and your wealth, to seek the Hereafter through them. al-Hasan said: Do not forget to seek, in this world, your sufficiency and wealth from what Allah has made lawful to you.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed me, saying: Hamid ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Harran [in the Isfahan manuscript: al-Khazzaz] related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Salama related to us, saying: Khalaf ibn Khalifa related to us, from Mansur ibn Zadhan, regarding His saying, "and do not forget your share of this world." He said: Your sustenance and the sustenance of your family. It was also said: It is the shroud, for that is his portion of this world when he departs from it.

**"And do good to people as Allah has done good to you, and do not seek corruption in the land. Indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters."** Qarun said: **"I was given this only on account of knowledge that is with me."** That is, on account of a superiority of knowledge that Allah taught me. He saw me as worthy of it, so He preferred me with this wealth over you, because of my superiority over you in knowledge and other things. It was also said: It is the knowledge of alchemy (al-kimya'). Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: Musa (peace be upon him) taught alchemy. He taught a third of that knowledge to Yusha' ibn Nun, a third to Kalib ibn Yufuna [in the Isfahan manuscript: Yufana], and Qarun received a third. Qarun then deceived them until he added their knowledge to his own. In another report: Allah, Exalted is He, taught Musa the knowledge of alchemy, and Musa taught his sister, and his sister taught Qarun, and this was the cause of his words. It was also said: It means knowledge of trading, agriculture, and all kinds of earning and seeking gain, that is with me. It was also said: It concerns the cause of his gathering those riches.

al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Abd Allah informed me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Halwani related to us, saying: Khuzayma ibn Ahmad related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi al-Jawari related to us, saying: I heard Abu Sulayman al-Darani say: Iblis (Satan) appeared to Qarun, and Qarun had remained on a mountain for forty years, worshipping. When he surpassed the Children of Israel in worship, Iblis sent his devils to him, but they could not overcome him. So Iblis himself appeared to him and began to worship as well. Qarun and Iblis competed in worship, and Iblis overpowered him and outdid him, so Qarun submitted to him. Iblis said to him: "O Qarun, we are content with what we are in, but do not witness any gathering of the Children of Israel, do not visit the sick, and do not attend any funeral." Then he brought him down from the mountain to the church, and they were brought food. Iblis said: "O Qarun, we are now content that it should be thus, depending on the Children of Israel." Qarun said to him: "Then what is your opinion?" He said: "Let us earn on Friday and worship for the rest of the Friday." So they earned on Friday and worshipped for the rest of Friday. Then Iblis said to Qarun: "We are content that it should be so." Qarun said to him: "Then what is your opinion?" He said: "Let us earn one day and worship one day, and give in charity and bestow." When they earned one day and worshipped one day, Iblis withdrew and left him, and the world was opened to Qarun, and his wealth grew.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Musa related to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Alawiya related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Musa related to us, from al-Musayyib ibn Shurayk, regarding "whose keys": he said: Their containers. They were four hundred thousand thousand [i.e., four hundred million], in forty sacks.

Allah, Exalted is He, said: **"Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him generations that were more powerful than him and greater in accumulation? And the guilty will not be asked about their sins"** [28:78]. Qatadah said: They will enter the Fire without reckoning. Mujahid said: That is, the angels will not ask about them, because they know them by their marks. al-Hasan said: "The guilty will not be asked about their sins" means that this is known from their predecessors, for if they are questioned, it is a question of rebuke and reproach.

**"So he went out before his people in his adornment"**: Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah [in the Isfahan manuscript: Hammad ibn 'Abd Allah] said: In crimson. al-Nakha'i and al-Hasan said: In red garments. Mujahid said: On white mules with saddles of purple (arjuwan) upon them, and they wore saffron-dyed garments (mu'asfarat). Qatadah said: On four thousand beasts, with them and upon their mounts purple cloth. Ibn Zayd said: With seventy thousand, wearing saffron-dyed garments. He said: That was the first day saffron-dyed garments were seen, as was related to us. Muqatil said: On a grey mule with a golden saddle upon which was purple cloth, and with him four thousand horsemen, and upon their mounts purple cloth, and with him three hundred white slave-girls adorned with jewelry, wearing red garments, on grey mules.

**"Those who desired the life of this world said: Oh, if only we had the like of what Qarun has been given! Indeed, he has a great portion [of wealth]."** **"But those who had been given knowledge said: Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds, and none is granted it except the patient"**, meaning those who are patient in obedience to Allah and in refraining from the adornments of this world.

**"So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home"**. The scholars of ancient reports said: Qarun was the most knowledgeable of the Children of Israel after Musa and Harun, and the most proficient in the Tawrat, and the most handsome and wealthiest of them. But he became a hypocrite like al-Samiri, and so he oppressed his people. The exegetes differed on the meaning of this oppression. Ibn 'Abbas said: Pharaoh had appointed Qarun over the Children of Israel when he was in Egypt. From al-Musayyib ibn Shurayk: he was an agent over the Children of Israel and used to wrong them. It was also said: He exceeded them in clothing by a span. It was said: He oppressed them through arrogance. It was said: Through the abundance of his wealth, for he was the richest and most prosperous of the people of his time. The exegetes differed on the number of the *'usba* in this place. Mujahid said: between ten and fifteen. Qatadah said: between ten and forty. 'Ikrimah said: some say forty and some say seventy. al-Dahhak said: between three and ten. It was said: they were sixty.

It is related from Khuthayma who said: I found in the Injil that the keys of Qarun's treasuries were a load for sixty white-faced mules with white markings, and no key exceeded a finger in size, and each key was for one treasure. It is said: Wherever he went, they were carried with him. They were of iron, but when they became heavy on him, he had them made of wood, and when these became heavy on him, he had them made of cowhide, the length of the fingers. They were carried with him on forty mules. The beginning of his transgression was that he became arrogant and lorded over the people through the abundance of his wealth. He would go out in his finery and strut, as Allah, Exalted is He, said: **"So he went out before his people in his adornment."**

Mujahid said: He went out on white mules with purple saddles, and they wore saffron-dyed garments. 'Abd al-Rahman said: He went out with seventy thousand, wearing saffron-dyed garments. Muqatil said: On a grey mule with a golden saddle upon which was purple cloth, and with him four thousand horsemen, with them and upon their mounts purple cloth, and with him three thousand white slave-girls adorned with jewelry, wearing red garments, on grey mules. So those of ignorance wished for the like of what he had been given, as Allah related. Then the people of knowledge of Allah admonished them: Fear Allah, for the reward of Allah **"is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds."**

He said: Then Allah revealed to His prophet Musa that he should command his people to attach to their cloaks four threads, with a green thread at each end, the color of which is like the color of the sky. Musa summoned the Children of Israel and said to them: Indeed, Allah, Exalted is He, commands you to attach to your cloaks green threads like the color of the sky, so that you may remember your Lord when you see them, and He, Exalted is He, sends down His speech upon you from the sky. Qarun became arrogant and said: These lords only do this to their servants, so that they may be distinguished from others.

When Musa (peace be upon him) brought the Children of Israel across the sea, he appointed al-Hibwara, which is the leadership of the altar and the house of offerings, to Harun. The Children of Israel would bring their gifts and hand them to Harun, who would place them on the altar, and a fire would descend from the sky and consume them. Qarun found this in himself, and he came to Musa and said: "O Musa, to you belongs the messengership, and to Harun the al-Hibwara, and you have nothing of this. I am more learned in the Tawrat than both of you, and I cannot bear this." Musa said: "By Allah, I did not give it to Harun; rather, Allah, Exalted is He, gave it to him." Qarun said: "By Allah, I will not believe you in this until you show me proof of it." So Musa (peace be upon him) gathered the leaders of the Children of Israel and said: "Bring me your staffs." They brought them, and he bound them together and placed them in his tent, where he worshipped Allah, Exalted is He, and they began to guard their staffs until morning. In the morning, Harun's staff had put forth green leaves, and it was from the leaves of an almond tree. Musa said: "O Qarun, do you see this?"

Qarun said: "By Allah, this is no more marvelous than the sorcery you practice."

Qarun left in anger, withdrew from Musa with his followers, and Musa kept dealing gently with him because of the kinship between them, while Qarun harmed him at all times and grew, every day, only in arrogance, defiance, and enmity toward Musa (peace be upon him). He built a house and made its door of gold, and he covered its walls with sheets of gold. The chiefs of the Children of Israel would go to him in the morning and in the evening; he fed them food, they conversed with him, and they laughed with him.

---

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 28, verses 76–88 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Abbas said: Then God, glory be to Him, revealed the zakat (obligatory alms) to Musa (peace be upon him). When God made zakat obligatory for them, Qarun refused. He reached an arrangement with them: for every thousand dinars, one dinar; for every thousand dirhams, one dirham; for every thousand sheep, one sheep; and for every thousand of anything, one of it. Then he returned to his house and calculated his wealth, and found it to be great. His soul would not allow him to give that up. So he gathered the Children of Israel and said to them: "O Children of Israel, Musa has commanded you in everything and you obeyed him, and now he wants to take your wealth." They said to him: "You are our elder and our master, so command us as you wish." He said: "I command you to bring me a certain prostitute, and we will give her a reward on condition that she accuses him of herself. When she does that, the Children of Israel will rise against him and abandon him, and we will be rid of him." So they brought her. Qarun gave her a thousand dirhams. It was also said: a thousand dinars; and it was said: a basin of gold; and it was said: her judgment (or her rule). He said to her: "I will enrich you and mix you with my women, on condition that you accuse Musa of having lain with you tomorrow, when the Children of Israel are present."

When the next day came, Qarun gathered the Children of Israel, then went to Musa and said to him: "The Children of Israel have gathered, waiting for you to come out, so that you may command them and forbid them, and explain to them the signs of their religion and the rulings of their law." Musa went out to them while they were in an open plain. He stood among them and preached, and among what he said in his admonition was: "O Children of Israel, whoever steals, we shall cut off his hand; whoever slanders, we shall flog him eighty lashes; whoever commits fornication while not married, we shall flog him a hundred lashes; and whoever commits fornication while married, we shall stone him until he dies." Qarun said to him: "Even if it is you?" He said: "Even if it is me." Qarun said: "The Children of Israel claim that you committed fornication with such-and-such a woman." He said: "I did?"
